title: Thyroid Storm
scenario: A 34-year-old female with a history of Graves' disease presents to the emergency department with high fever, palpitations, agitation, and confusion two days after stopping her methimazole for a respiratory infection.

lines: 34-year-old female brought in by partner for high fever, racing heart, tremor, and confusion. History of Graves' disease; stopped methimazole 5 days ago during a chest infection. Skin hot and diaphoretic. Fine tremor of the hands. Restless and agitated, oriented to person only. Eyes prominent with lid lag.
IV access obtained. Labs and 12-lead ECG ordered. Cardiac monitor applied showing rapid irregular rhythm. Cooling measures started. 2L O2 per nasal cannula applied.
Provider notified of findings. Propranolol, propylthiouracil (PTU), and hydrocortisone administered per order. Cooling blanket applied. Acetaminophen given for fever.
Client calmer and oriented x3. Temperature down to 100.4 F. Heart rate slowed to 108 and regular. Tremor diminished. Reports feeling less anxious.
Methimazole 10 mg PO daily (self-discontinued 5 days ago)
Administer propranolol 1 mg IV, titrate to heart rate
Apply cooling blanket; acetaminophen 650 mg PO for fever
Notify provider for temperature > 104 F or worsening mental status

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.rationale: Hyperpyrexia, marked tachyarrhythmia, altered mentation, and tremor are hallmark decompensating features of thyroid storm requiring urgent intervention. Exophthalmos and a near-normal SpO2 are less acutely dangerous.

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.stem: For each finding, click to specify whether it reflects increased metabolic activity, cardiovascular effect, or both. Each finding may reflect more than one.
children.rationale: Excess thyroid hormone raises the metabolic rate (fever, elevated T4) and stimulates the heart (tachycardia, widened pulse pressure). Tachycardia is driven by both the hypermetabolic state and direct cardiac stimulation.

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.stem: Complete the sentence. The nurse determines that the priority problem is {1}, and the most immediate goal is to {2}.

choices.text: reduce the fever and control the heart rate

children.rationale: In thyroid storm the immediate threats are hyperpyrexia and cardiovascular collapse, so the priority goal is lowering temperature and controlling the tachyarrhythmia. Nutrition and rest matter but are not the acute priority.

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.stem: For each intervention, click to specify whether it is indicated or contraindicated for this client.

rows.text: Administer propranolol to control heart rate
Encourage the client to ambulate in the hallway

children.rationale: Beta-blockade, antithyroid drugs, and active cooling are core treatments. Aspirin is contraindicated because it displaces thyroid hormone from binding proteins and raises free levels; exertion increases metabolic demand and is contraindicated.

children.subject: Pharmacology
children.stem: After giving propranolol, PTU, and hydrocortisone, which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.

options.text: Continuously monitor cardiac rhythm and heart rate
Monitor temperature frequently and continue cooling measures
Assess blood pressure for hypotension after propranolol
Administer amiodarone as first-line for the fever

children.rationale: The nurse monitors the rhythm, temperature, and blood pressure response to therapy. Warming would worsen hyperthermia, and amiodarone is not a treatment for fever.

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.stem: Which findings indicate the treatment has been effective? Select all that apply.

options.text: Heart rate slowed to 108 and regular

children.rationale: Falling temperature, a slower regular heart rate, improved mentation, and reduced tremor all show the storm is resolving. A persistently widened pulse pressure would indicate ongoing instability, not improvement.
